chunks: Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from ʿAbbād ibn Sulaymān, from Saʿd ibn Saʿd, from Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام:

Regarding a well between which and a latrine there are five cubits, or less, or more: may wudu (ablution) be performed from it? He عليه السلام said: “It is not disliked whether near or far; wudu (ablution) may be performed from it and ghusl may be done with it so long as the water has not changed.”
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This report indicates that all the preceding reports are to be understood as referring to recommendation, not prohibition and obligation.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well from which water is drawn
key_terms.الْكَنِيفِ: the latrine or privy near the well

ai.seo_question: Can wudu (ablution) and ghusl be performed from a well near a latrine if the water has not changed?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of using water from a well located near a latrine. It states that wudu (ablution) and ghusl are permissible from such water so long as the water has not undergone change, and the compiler notes that earlier reports are to be understood as recommending caution rather than establishing prohibition or obligation.
